angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 737,442 km at 176.73 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6585 +/- 0.0103 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 176.73 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.06 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Serrano Bell et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1273 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A...6S/abstract): 737,442 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.06 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Serrano Bell et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1273 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A...6S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5690 +/- 40 K from Serrano Bell et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1273 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A...6S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Serrano Bell et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1273 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A...6S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1273.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.413, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
